title: Designing Cooling and Airflow
summary: Balance heat, airflow, monitoring, and resource use in a conceptual cooling design.
objectives: Connect computing heat to airflow and monitoring choices.
Identify a cooling tradeoff in a simple design comparison.

vocab.def: Using resources carefully to achieve a needed result.
The place where air enters a system.
The place where warmer or used air leaves a system.

sections.heading: Cooling is part of the design
sections.body: Computing equipment produces heat. A design must move heat away using planned intake, airflow, exhaust, and temperature monitoring.

sections.heading: Every choice has a tradeoff
sections.body: More cooling capacity may support reliability but use more energy or resources. A compact arrangement may save space but make airflow harder. Designers compare needs instead of choosing by one number.

sections.heading: Improve a diagram
sections.body: Add arrows to a paper layout showing cool-air intake and warm-air exhaust. Mark a blocked path and explain one improvement. Do not service HVAC machinery or open energized equipment.

practice.prompt: Two layouts use the same equipment. Layout A has clear intake and exhaust paths. Layout B sends warm exhaust back toward an intake. Which risk should the team investigate?

quiz.question: What should a cooling design balance?
options: Heat movement, reliability, and resource use
Only the color of the equipment
A guarantee that equipment never needs power
quiz.answer: Heat movement, reliability, and resource use

reflectionPrompt: What cooling choice could improve reliability while creating a resource question?
